title: VeriPol flags 25 and 39 false robbery reports in Murcia and Málaga in a one-week 2017 pilot; Spain's police drop it in 2024
summary: The Spanish National Police's text-based false-report classifier flagged 25 false robberies in Murcia and 39 in Málaga in a week in June 2017 (versus 3 and 12 in the same month over the prior decad...
account: VeriPol, a model for detecting false robbery reports from their text, was developed by researchers from the Complutense and Carlos III universities with police officer Miguel Camacho-Collados and published in Knowledge-Based Systems (Quijano-Sánchez, Liberatore, Camacho-Collados and Camacho-Collados, 2018); the abstract reports a validation accuracy of 91% on more than 1,000 reports from 2015, an improvement of more than 15% over expert officers, and a pilot study in June 2017 showing a lower bound on empirical precision of about 83%. Scientific American (1 February 2019) reported that the one-week pilot in Murcia and Málaga detected 25 and 39 false robberies respectively, against 3 and 12 in the same month over the previous decade, and quoted Camacho Collados on colleagues wasting time on cases that never occurred. Civio (25 March 2025) reported that the police said that in 83.54% of reports flagged false the complainant confessed, that the Interior Ministry announced nationwide use in 2018, that 49,702 complaints were analyzed in 2019 with 2,338 deemed false and 3,762 in 2022 with 511 deemed false, and that use stopped on 21 October 2024 because the tool was not valid in judicial proceedings; a University of Valencia report (September 2024) criticized the 1,122-report training sample, missing officer training and regional language variation. AlgorithmWatch (27 October 2020) found no independent verification of effectiveness since deployment. The pilot month carries no day, so Scientific American's publication date is used.
purpose: Estimate the probability that a robbery report is false from its text to support police decisions.
developer: Researchers at Universidad Complutense de Madrid and Universidad Carlos III de Madrid with Spanish National Police officer Miguel Camacho-Collados
deployer: Spanish National Police (Policía Nacional), Ministry of the Interior
segment: False robbery reports filed with police
taxonomy_note: Loose fit; the flagged false reports are fraud detected after filing, and independent sources document the absence of evaluation and the 2024 discontinuation.

ratings.reason: Flagged-report counts and confession rates are police aggregates with no independent confirmation.
No measured effect on insurance fraud or police resources is documented.

ai_role.statement: The peer-reviewed paper describes a natural-language-processing and machine-learning classifier with L1 feature selection that outputs the probability a report is false; the paper's authors include the police developer, and AlgorithmWatch and Civio report that no independent verification was done before the police stopped using it in October 2024.

produced_by: Training on 1,122 robbery reports from 2015 (534 genuine, 588 false) labeled by one experienced officer
Text features selected by L1 penalization plus heuristic rules, scoring reports at the police station
must_hold: Reports written in the same language register as the training data (the Valencia report faulted missing regional variation)
Officer training and protocols for acting on scores
Independent field evaluation, absent before discontinuation

echoes.source: AlgorithmWatch and Civio: 49,702 complaints analysed, 2,338 flagged false, no verification
Civio: use stopped; Ministry said the tool is not valid in judicial proceedings

headline: VeriPol flags 25 and 39 false robberies in Murcia and Málaga
metric: 25 and 39 false robberies respectively, against 3 and 12 in the same month

comparator.against: false robbery reports detected by officers in the same month over the previous decade
comparator.before: only three and 12, respectively, for that month in the previous decade
comparator.after: 25 and 39 false robberies in just one week
comparator.quote: A June 2017 pilot test in the cities of Murcia and Málaga helped to detect 25 and 39 false robberies in just one week—compared with only three and 12, respectively, for that month in the previous decade.

later.note: Civio reported that the National Police stopped using VeriPol in October 2024 (day not given) because, the Interior Ministry said, it lacks validity in judicial proceedings.
later.quote: In October 2024, six years later, the National Police stopped using the AI, the Technical Office of the Directorate General of Police has told Civio. The Ministry of the Interior stated that the reason for rejecting its use is that it lacks validity in judicial proceedings.

revisions.change: Record drafted from the cited sources.
Benefit type set to Reduced Risk under Trustible's full taxonomy of 23 types; it was Improved Organizational Efficiency among the six first used.
Added what the benefit is measured against, what happened since from the cited sources.

claim_basis: Four independent news reports and the makers' peer-reviewed study are on file. There is no independent study or report and no finding by a regulator or court.
